rule: every line a quote; source: and consent: travel with it. Books in chronological order of the operator's anchor year — the poet first, then the giants whose shoulders were climbed. A missing cover gets a dark cover with the title in light.

books.author: Walt Whitman
books.title: Leaves of Grass
books.anchor: 1855 — Leaves of Grass. We need poets first.
books.source: Song of Myself and the Preface, Leaves of Grass (1855) — public domain; read from the Feuilles d'herbe edition (trad. Éric Athenot) on the operator's shelf
books.note: jnxmas, 2026-08-29: and this works for any western country, still now.
lines: I celebrate myself, and what I assume you shall assume,
For every atom belonging to me as good belongs to you.
America does not repel the past or what it has produced under its forms…
accepts the lesson with calmness…
I am large, I contain multitudes.

books.author: Lance Gutteridge
books.title: Avoiding IT Disasters
books.anchor: 1970 — the first reference in the book: where enterprise systems start failing.
books.source: Avoiding IT Disasters — cover subtitle and dedication, first page, transcribed from the physical book by jnxmas, 2026-08-29
lines: Fallacies about enterprise systems, and how you can rise above them.
I dedicate this book to all the people who have been harmed by enterprise software systems;
you deserve better.

books.author: Eliyahu M. Goldratt
books.title: Le But
books.anchor: 2013 — the AFNOR edition; the facts follow the industrial revolution: Toyota, Hitachi — the 1970s, 80s, 90s.
books.source: The Goal (Goldratt & Cox, 1984), short attributed quotations; prologue to « Debout sur les épaules des géants », Le But, AFNOR édition spéciale — transcribed from the physical book by jnxmas, 2026-08-29
lines: An hour lost at a bottleneck is an hour lost for the entire system.
Tell me how you measure me, and I will tell you how I will behave.
La bonne définition d'un but est celle qui nous met sur le chemin de l'amélioration continue.
Pour atteindre un tel but, une percée décisive ne suffit pas. En fait, il en faut beaucoup.
Vingt-cinq ans après avoir écrit Le But, le Dr Goldratt écrivait « Debout sur les épaules des géants ».

lines: Carpe diem.
O Captain! my Captain!
That the powerful play goes on, and you may contribute a verse.
What will your verse be?

books.author: Satoshi Nakamoto
books.title: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
books.edition: the whitepaper, 2008 — four constraints, one solution
books.source: Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (2008), §2–6 and §11 — the constraints are named by the realm (Goldratt's question), the solutions are the paper's own words; the whitepaper is published under the MIT license
books.consent: MIT license, attributed; the constraint half of each line is ours
books.note: jnxmas, 2026-08-29: the paper that moved me into the magic of mathematics — how not to…
lines: Double-spending, with no trusted party → a public chain of timestamped blocks: « the only way to confirm the absence of a transaction is to be aware of all transactions. »
Who may vote, when identities are free → proof-of-work: « one-CPU-one-vote »; to rewrite history, redo the work.
Agreement in a room anyone can enter → the longest chain: « proof that it came from the largest pool of CPU power. »
Why anyone would run it honestly → the reward: « more profitable to play by the rules … than to undermine the system and the validity of his own wealth. »
